name: RHA fillers (Teoxane)
lead: RHA (Resilient Hyaluronic Acid) fillers are cross-linked hyaluronic acid (HA) products from the Swiss company Teoxane, marketed as Teosyal RHA outside the US and RHA Redensity in the US. They were developed to hold up in dynamic areas of the face that move with expression, such as around the mouth. [1][2]
Controlled trials report effectiveness of RHA Redensity for dynamic perioral lines, and trials have studied infraorbital hollows, lips and nasolabial folds. [1][3][4][5]
infobox: Gel that stretches with facial movement

paras: The RHA range uses a manufacturing process meant to preserve long HA chains so the gel stays flexible and resilient in motion. [1] Laboratory work has compared injectability of commercial cross-linked HA fillers [6] and compared cross-linking technologies. [7] Technique articles describe midface volumization with RHA gels. [8]
A case report describes a hypersensitivity reaction to an RHA filler. [9] A multidose hyaluronidase study examined degradation of RHA fillers in vitro. [10]

A 52-week randomized, evaluator-blinded, no-treatment-controlled study evaluated RHA Redensity for moderate-to-severe dynamic perioral rhytides. [1] A prospective registry reported one-year effectiveness and safety of HA fillers in routine practice, and a real-world periorbital study has been published. [11][12] A retrospective study used ultrasound to assess skin density after treatment with an HA-based hydrogel. [13]

Registered trials include perioral rhytids (n=202), infraorbital hollows (n=248; China study recruiting), lips versus Restylane-L (n=202) and nasolabial folds against Juvéderm Ultra XC (n=148) and Perlane-L (n=140). [3][4][5][14][15]

lore.intro: RHA fillers receive little forum discussion in the community material reviewed.

card.summary: Teoxane's flexible HA gels built for moving areas like the mouth, with randomized perioral and under-eye trials.
card.note: Thin community discussion; a hypersensitivity case report exists.

quick.overview:
RHA fillers are hyaluronic acid gels designed to flex with facial movement, used around the mouth, lips and under eyes.

A 52-week randomized study reported benefit for dynamic perioral lines.
quick.mechanism: A cross-linked HA gel retaining long HA chains adds soft volume and stretches with expression; hyaluronidase dissolves it.
quick.risks: Reported effects include swelling and bruising; hypersensitivity has been reported. Prescription device given by licensed clinicians.
